- OpenAI shipped **GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol** on 17 November, cutting Astra's input and output prices 20% and calling Astra its first released model to meet its "High" bar for AI self-improvement (Section 1).
- Microsoft packed **seven new MAI models** into Ignite 2026, betting enterprises will trade a little peak capability for a much lower cost per task (Section 1).

- **Nvidia** reported record quarterly revenue of **$115.8 billion** but told investors its outlook excludes China compute revenue after halting Hopper data-centre shipments there (Section 6).
- The **United States** moved to close the overseas-data-centre route to advanced AI chips, tightening controls on remote access (Section 6).

- **Sam Altman, OpenAI (2026-11-16):** At Semafor's *Silicon Valley & The World* event he said the AI industry "will be fine" without Jensen Huang, that he has "personal strong empathy" for him, and declined to say whether Huang should return. - **Tom Brown, Anthropic (2026-11-16–17):** The co-founder and chief compute officer, in IPO roadshow material reported by Tom's Hardware, said Anthropic's Claude Mythos got Claude running on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days — writing "almost 100% of the kernels" — a task he estimated would previously take six to twelve months. The three days cover prompt processing for one model, the baseline is Anthropic's own estimate, and no AMD-versus-Nvidia performance data has been published. Sources: [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-says-claude-mythos-slashed-software-work-to-onboard-amd-gpus-from-up-to-12-months-to-around-three-days-writing-almost-100-percent-of-kernels-autonomously-chips-away-at-nvidias-cuda-moat) · [AIToolsRecap](https://aitoolsrecap.com/Blog/anthropic-mythos-amd-mi355x-three-day-port).

## 6. Other Material AI Industry News
- **2026-11-16–17 — AMD closes two AI acquisitions totalling about $11.1 billion:** AMD said it completed its all-stock acquisition of **World Labs**, the spatial-intelligence lab led by **Fei-Fei Li**, valued at about **$8.2 billion** when announced on 28 September, and named Li executive vice president and chief scientist reporting to CEO Lisa Su; a day later it closed its acquisition of **Taalas**, a Toronto maker of model-specific inference chips, valued at roughly **$2.9 billion** in a 4 November filing. AMD plans to fold Taalas' technology into its accelerator roadmap alongside Instinct GPUs. Sources: [AMD — World Labs](https://newsroom.amd.com/news/amd-completes-acquisition-world-labs/) · [AMD IR](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1306/amd-completes-acquisition-of-world-labs) · [AMD — Taalas](https://newsroom.amd.com/news/amd-completes-acquisition-taalas-advance-ai-inference-innovation/) · [Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/amd-closes-taalas-deal-to-add-model-specific-ai-inference-chips/).
- **2026-11-17 — Nvidia reports record quarter and a post-Huang reset:** Nvidia posted third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of **$115.8 billion**, up 103% year over year, with data-centre revenue of **$107.6 billion**; interim CEO Colette Kress said the company has stopped shipping licensed Hopper data-centre products to China and that its roughly **$130 billion** forecast for next quarter excludes China compute revenue. Separately, Nvidia said it does not plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO while it runs its search, and the SEC is reportedly investigating the company. Sources: [Nvidia](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-third-quarter-fiscal-2027) · [TechCrunch — succession](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-says-it-doesnt-plan-to-reappoint-jensen-huang-as-ceo/) · [TechCrunch — China](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-is-abandoning-china-after-jensen-huangs-ouster/) · [TechCrunch — SEC](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/sec-reportedly-investigating-nvidia-amid-huang-exit/).
- **2026-11-16 — US moves to restrict remote access to advanced AI chips:** The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule requiring licences to send advanced semiconductors to data centres in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, tightening checks on foundries and packagers and formally scrapping the earlier AI Diffusion Rule; operators in the five countries reportedly have 90 days to comply. Sources: [Pillsbury](https://www.pillsburylaw.com/en/news-and-insights/commerce-restricts-remote-access-advanced-chips.html) · [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-16/us-moves-to-limit-remote-access-to-advanced-ai-chips) · [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/16/us-tightens-ai-chip-export-controls-to-deter-chinese-companies-from-accessing-compute-remotely/) · [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/trump-china-ai-chip-loophole.html).

## Editorial Notes
- **Recovery items:** None. Every item above was first announced or materially updated between 2026-11-16T07:38:52Z and 2026-11-18T07:38:52Z; no pre-window backfill is included.
- **Vendor claims:** Pricing, benchmark and capability figures in Sections 1–3 are the developers' or authors' own unless a named third party is cited. HeyGen's "84.4% indistinguishable" figure, Microsoft's benchmark comparisons and OpenAI's benchmark numbers are the vendors' own; Anthropic's six-to-twelve-month porting baseline is its own estimate.
- **Papers:** Section 2 items were posted to arXiv on 17 November 2026. Only the agent-governance paper is peer-reviewed (accepted, NeurIPS 2026); the rest are non-peer-reviewed preprints. The LMMR figures are the authors' own.
- **Project metrics:** GitHub star totals and 24-hour deltas come from GitDiscover read 2026-11-18 UTC; they move quickly and are directional. Entries marked "See repo" have no single verified top-level licence.
- **Date caveats:** Tencent dates Hy4 flash to 16 November, but the press release time is not shown, so it sits at the very edge of the window. The AMD World Labs completion and Nvidia's results are dated to their own releases (16 and 17 November).
- **Unverified / reported:** Nvidia's SEC investigation is press-reported and unconfirmed by the company. The $2.9 billion Taalas value is AMD's own filing estimate.
